Actually we need the aniline nitrogen attached to sulfonyl, not piperazine. The piperazine is attached to aromatic via a side chain (N2CCN...). In SMILES, the aromatic ring has substituent N2CCN(...). That's a side chain attached via nitrogen to aromatic carbon (anilide). So the aromatic carbon is attached to N of piperazine (aryl-N). So we need to form C-N bond between aromatic carbon and piperazine nitrogen. That's a Buchwald amination of aryl bromide with piperazine (protected). So step 2: aryl bromide + Boc-piperazine -> aryl-N(piperazine-Boc). Use template maybe 1258606? Not sure.

Step 3: Deprotect Boc to give final piperazine with carbamate (tert-butyl carbonate) still present? Actually final has C(OC(C)(C)C)=O attached to piperazine nitrogen (carbamate). That's a tert-butyl carbamate on the piperazine nitrogen (N-COOtBu). So we need to install that after deprotection? Actually final has N(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O) meaning the piperazine nitrogen is carbamoylated with tBu carbonate. So we need to protect piperazine with Boc (tert-butoxycarbonyl) which is exactly that group. So the Boc group is present in final. So we don't need deprotection; the Boc is part of final. So step 2 yields final product after sulfonylation.

Thus route: Step A (Buchwald amination) to attach Boc-piperazine to aryl bromide -> gives aryl-N(piperazine-Boc). Step B (sulfonylation) of the aniline (the aryl-N) with 4-fluorobenzenesulfonyl chloride to give final product.

That's 2 steps.
